did_you_know.text: In verses 1–4, God asks Job whether he knows when the mountain goats and does give birth and whether he watches the process of their delivery.
The text emphasizes that pregnancy lasts for months, but people do not know the exact time when wild animals will give birth.
The young of the mountain goats and does grow up in the wild, become strong, leave on their own, and do not return to their parents.
The wild donkey is portrayed as free: God is the one who set it free and released its restraints, meaning that it is not subject to human control.
The wild donkey keeps away from the noise of the city, roams the mountains, and searches for every green plant for food.
The wild ox is presented as a powerful animal, but one that will not agree to work for humans or spend the night in their stall.
Job is asked whether he can harness the wild ox to a plow or make it plow the valleys behind him; these questions emphasize its independence and the impossibility of using it as a working animal.
In verses 13–18, a bird is described as laying its eggs on the ground and warming them in the dust, leaving the eggs exposed to dangers from the surrounding environment.
The war horse is described as courageous, with a mane and a terrifying snort; the description emphasizes its strength and eagerness for battle.
The hawk is described as spreading its wings and flying south, and the text presents its migration as a phenomenon beyond human understanding.
